grammar.title: Inversi untuk penekanan
grammar.explanation: Setelah ungkapan negatif atau pembatas di awal kalimat (Not only, Rarely, Never before, Only after), urutan subjek dan kata bantu dibalik seperti pertanyaan. Gaya ini membuat tulisan akademik dan esai beasiswa terdengar matang, tapi jangan dipakai berlebihan.
examples: Not only did I lead the team, but I also trained two new developers.
Rarely have I seen a problem affect so many users.
Only after the launch did we realise how serious the issue was.

common_mistake.wrong: Not only I led the project, but I also managed the budget.
common_mistake.right: Not only did I lead the project, but I also managed the budget.

grammar.title: Cleft sentence: what ... is / it was ... that
grammar.explanation: Cleft sentence memfokuskan perhatian pada satu bagian kalimat. 'What + klausa + is' menonjolkan hal yang dimaksud; 'It was ... that ...' menonjolkan penyebab atau pelaku. Setelah 'is', kata kerja memakai bentuk dasar dengan 'to' atau -ing, bukan campuran keduanya.
examples: What motivates me is the chance to make technology fairer.
It was my grandmother's struggle with her phone that made me interested in accessibility.
What I need now is formal research training.

common_mistake.wrong: What I want is to studying accessibility.
common_mistake.right: What I want is to study accessibility.

reading.title: What admissions committees actually look for
reading.text: Every year, admissions committees at competitive universities read thousands of personal statements, and most of them sound remarkably similar. Applicants describe themselves as passionate, hard-working and eager to learn, yet rarely provide evidence for any of these claims. What distinguishes a memorable statement is not impressive vocabulary but a coherent narrative. The strongest essays usually begin with a specific moment that sparked the applicant's interest, then show how that interest was tested and deepened through study or work. Crucially, they explain why this particular programme is the logical next step, referring to courses, researchers or facilities by name. Committees are also alert to statements that have clearly been polished by someone else, or generated with little personal input; such essays tend to lack the small, concrete details that only the writer could know. In short, readers are not looking for a perfect candidate, but for a credible one whose goals are realistic and whose story hangs together.

questions.q: What do many personal statements lack, according to the text?

options: With a specific moment that sparked an interest

questions.q: What kind of candidate are committees looking for?
options: A credible candidate with realistic goals

writing.prompt: Tulis bagian inti personal statement untuk beasiswa S2 (misalnya LPDP atau Chevening). Ceritakan momen yang memicu minatmu, bagaimana pengalamanmu memperdalamnya, kenapa program ini yang kamu pilih, dan dampak yang ingin kamu ciptakan setelah lulus.
checklist: Dibuka dengan momen spesifik, bukan kalimat klise
Minimal satu inversi atau cleft sentence
Rencana setelah lulus yang realistis dan terukur
useful_phrases: Not only did I ..., but I also ...
writing.model_answer:
It was a Sunday afternoon when my grandmother handed me her phone, close to tears, because she could not find the button to pay her electricity bill. The app had been redesigned the week before, and a feature she had used for years was now hidden behind three unlabelled icons. What struck me was not the inconvenience itself, but how quickly she concluded that the problem was her own fault.

That moment changed the way I approach my work as a web developer. Over the past four years, I have built features used by more than two million customers, but I have also started to ask who our products leave out. Not only did I introduce accessibility checks into our release process, but I also organised the company's first interviews with users over sixty. In light of what we learned, the team simplified the payment flow, and complaints from older customers fell by nearly forty percent.

Practical experience, however, has its limits. I can fix individual screens, yet I lack the research methods needed to understand why certain groups struggle and how to design for them systematically. This is why the programme in Human-Computer Interaction appeals to me so strongly. Its modules on inclusive design and its research group on ageing and technology would equip me with exactly the skills I am missing.

After graduating, I intend to return to Indonesia, where the number of older internet users is growing rapidly, yet they remain underrepresented in product research. My goal is to help local companies adopt inclusive design guidelines, so that the next time someone like my grandmother opens an app, it works for her too.

speaking.prompt: IELTS Speaking Part 3 atau wawancara beasiswa: 'Should universities focus on preparing students for jobs, or on knowledge for its own sake?' Beri jawaban seimbang dengan pendapat yang jelas (6 sampai 8 kalimat).
speaking.sample_answer: I'd say universities have to do both, although the balance depends on the subject. On the one hand, students invest a huge amount of time and money, so it's reasonable for them to expect skills that employers value. On the other hand, if universities only trained people for today's jobs, graduates would struggle when those jobs change, which in technology happens every few years. What employers increasingly ask for, in my experience, is the ability to think critically and learn quickly, and that comes from deep knowledge rather than narrow training. So rather than choosing one side, I think universities should teach fundamentals rigorously and connect them to real projects. That way, students leave with both understanding and practical experience.

n1.them: Let's start with something challenging. Tell us about a time you failed.

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "Last year I launched a feature without testing it with older users. What I learned was that assumptions are expensive."

n2.them: And what did you do differently afterwards?
hints: inversi: Not only did I ..., but I also ...

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "Not only did I start running user interviews, but I also added accessibility checks to every release."

n3.them: Many applicants have stronger academic records than you. Why should we choose you?
hints: akui dengan elegan, lalu tonjolkan pengalaman

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "While my grades are good rather than perfect, I bring four years of practical experience and evidence of real impact on users."

n4.them: Suppose you couldn't return to work in Indonesia straight after graduating. What would you do?

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "I would still contribute remotely, for example by mentoring local designers, and return as soon as I could."

n5.them: Final question: in one sentence, what impact do you hope to have in ten years?
hints: pakai tangible atau bridge the gap

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "I hope to have helped Indonesian companies make their products usable for millions of people who are currently left out."

end.them: Thank you, Bagus. That was a very thoughtful interview. You'll hear from us next month.
